Hi Priya,

Thanks for the kickoff call yesterday. As we prepare the CloudFolio marketplace listing, Legal and Ops want to confirm how Redwood will handle data residency, retention, and deletion across the three major cloud vendors (AWS/GCP/Azure) for EU customers. A few concrete asks to unblock our internal review: 

- Can you confirm where embeddings and model interaction logs will be stored for customers who select an "EU-only" hosting option on AWS, GCP, and Azure?
- What retention windows are configurable per-customer? We need an option for 30/90/365 days and a guaranteed immediate deletion workflow on contract termination.
- How do cross-region fallbacks work (e.g., if EU capacity is exhausted, will requests route to non-EU or to a compatible model variant)? We need clarity for our listing copy and for compliance.

I've attached our onboarding brief with the partner requirements. Can you loop in engineering / legal if needed?

Thanks,
Lindsey Park

Subject: Re: Marketplace listing — residency & retention questions

Hi Lindsey — great questions, thanks for the level of detail. High-level answers below; I included Marissa (Marketplace) and Ben (Dedicated/Private) for follow-up on config and SLAs.

1) Storage locations by cloud (EU customers):
   - AWS: embeddings + ephemeral request logs are kept in eu-west-1 by default for EU-only accounts.
   - GCP: eu-west1 (or eu region) storage for embeddings; request logs are routed to the configured EU GCP project.
   - Azure: we support West Europe (Netherlands) and can support Germany West Central if customers require DE-unique residency.

2) Retention windows: configurable per-customer. Out-of-the-box options: 30 / 90 / 365 / custom (up to 5 years). We expose retention policy at the tenant level in the Console and via API. Deletion workflow: we offer immediate deletion trigger + background purge which completes within 72 hours for indexed artifacts; full physical scrub from backups within our standard retention window (up to 30 days for cold backups) unless overridden by an enterprise SLA.

3) Cross-region fallback: by default policy is "region-first, model-fallback" — requests are routed to EU capacity; if EU capacity is exhausted we will fallback to a compatible model variant in the nearest data region in the same jurisdiction when possible. For customers that require strict region-lock (no cross-region execution), we support a "no-fallback" policy at account provisioning.

Items for us to confirm internally and send as a short summary:
- Exact SLO for background purge from backups (Ben to confirm).
- Documentation snippet for region-lock configuration in the Console (Marissa to add to listing copy).

I'll follow up with a one-pager and link to the console tenant settings.

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Short vendor statement (for marketplace listing / vendor risk assessment):
- Data storage by cloud (EU-only): AWS: eu-west-1; GCP: eu-west1 / EU region; Azure: West Europe by default, Germany West Central available for DE-only needs.
- Retention options: tenant-level configurable: 30 / 90 / 365 / custom (up to 5 years).
- Deletion: Immediate deletion trigger removes indexed artifacts within 72 hours; full purge from cold backups occurs per our backup retention policy (default 30 days). Enterprise SLA exceptions (shorter backup purge) available on contract.
- Cross-region execution: default behavior is region-first with model-fallback; a "no-fallback" region-lock option prevents cross-region execution when enabled at provisioning.
